item.title: Michael McCloskey Has Died. He Helped Make the Sierra Club a Political Force.
item.description: As executive director of the group from 1969 to 1985, he aligned its disparate local chapters and offices into a powerful lobby in Washington. He was 92.
item.dc:creator: Keith Schneider
item.media:description: Michael McCloskey in an undated photo. By the time he retired from the Sierra Club, it was regarded as a titan of grass-roots environmental activism nationally.

item.title: Stacy Keach, Actor Who Embodied Hamlet and Mike Hammer, Dies at 85
item.description: He missed out on several major film roles, but found steady work in the theater, on TV and in movies.
item.dc:creator: Barry Singer
item.media:description: Stacy Keach as Mike Hammer in 1984. “If a script interests me,” he wrote in his memoir, “or a character intrigues me, or the cast features someone I’ve always wanted to work with, or the location is somewhere exotic, then sign me up.”

item.title: He Made a Game of Chance. His Obituary Is a Game, Too.
item.description: Steve Selvin has died. To understand his significance, try to wrap your head around the Monty Hall Problem.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen, Amisha Padnani and Hang Do Thi Duc
item.media:credit: Photo Illustration by The New York Times; photos via Getty images

item.title: Stanley Zabar Has Died. He Managed the Books, and the Slaw, at an N.Y.C. Landmark.
item.description: Zabar’s, a family business, became a renowned food emporium, which he ran with his brother Saul and another partner. He was 94.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir

item.title: Isabel Letelier, a Chilean Voice for Human Rights, Has Died
item.description: Her husband, a prominent figure in the government of Salvador Allende, was assassinated in Washington in 1976. She was 94.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir
item.category: Human Rights and Human Rights Violations
Coups D'Etat and Attempted Coups D'Etat

item.title: Gary Fisketjon Has Died. He Edited Ellis, Tartt, McInerney and McCarthy.
item.description: A champion of slow, methodical editing and long working relationships with writers, he was regarded as one of the best of his generation. He was 72.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen

item.title: Tony Butala, Member of the Lettermen, Has Died
item.description: His squeaky-clean vocal trio, the Lettermen, survived the Beatles and Jimi Hendrix to pepper the pop charts with lush, retro-tinged songs. He was 87.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams

item.title: The Oldest Person to Complete New York City Marathon Has Died at 104
item.description: Jonathan de Sola Mendes, a decorated Marine Corps aviator, was 96 when he crossed the finish line in 2016. Then he sipped some Johnnie Walker Black Label.
item.dc:creator: Jeré Longman
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces

item.title: How the New York Times Obituaries Desk Covers Death by Suicide
item.description: There is more openness about discussing suicide now. But sometimes families talk about it only reluctantly, or not at all.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:credit: Photo Illustrations by Leslie dela Vega/The New York Times; Photographs, via Getty Images

item.title: Richard Holmes, Who Integrated Mississippi State University, Has Died
item.description: When he stepped onto campus in 1965, he said, he was met with “curiosity and disbelief.”
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir

item.title: They Found Love Late in Life, and Then Died Within Weeks of Each Other
item.description: Marjorie Shelley, an arts conservator, and Doug Adams, an outdoorsman, discovered they were kindred spirits. She was 81; he was 71.
item.dc:creator: Penelope Green

item.title: Richard Aurelio Has Died. He Helped Re-elect Mayor Lindsay.
item.description: A political and public relations virtuoso and journalist, he also worked for Senator Jacob Javits and brought an all-news cable channel to New York. He was 98.
item.dc:creator: Sam Roberts
item.media:description: Mr. Aurelio at the Lindsay campaign headquarters in New York City in 1972.

item.title: Lloyd Geering, Pastor Who Disputed Christ’s Resurrection, Dies at 108
item.description: “It is faith that man needs, not past doctrines,” he said in defense of his views, which became a cause célèbre for many but were condemned by others.
item.dc:creator: Alan Cowell

item.title: Michael Ward Stout, Lawyer Who Ran Mapplethorpe’s Foundation, Has Died
item.description: He became immersed in the art world through Salvador Dalí and worked with several artists’ foundations and estates. He was 83.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir

item.title: The Washington Post’s First Black Masthead Editor Has Died
item.description: Milton Coleman was centrally involved in two major stories in the 1980s that raised questions of journalism ethics. He was 79.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nossiter

item.title: Richard Lloyd, Torrential Guitarist of Television, Has Died
item.description: With Tom Verlaine, he led the dual-guitar attack in a band that brought fiery yet sophisticated art rock to the New York City punk scene of the 1970s. He was 75.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams
item.media:description: Richard Lloyd performing with Television in London in 1977.

item.title: Sinclair Clark Made Museum Masterpieces. Why Was His Name Left Out?
item.description: As a taxidermy tanner, he prepared the thick, heavy skins of majestic creatures for display in museums across the world. But for a long time, he went unnamed.
item.dc:creator: Gordon K. Hurd

item.title: Lonnie Thompson Has Died. He Dodged Avalanches to Preserve Climate History.
item.description: His observations helped establish shriveling mountain glaciers as an unmistakable consequence of human-caused warming. He was 78.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong

item.title: Martin Blinder Has Died. He Was Blamed for the ‘Twinkie Defense.’
item.description: A forensic psychiatrist, he testified that consuming sugary foods could cause antisocial behavior. To his dismay, a catchphrase was born. He was 89.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen

item.title: John D. Rockefeller IV, West Virginia Governor and Senator, Dies at 89
item.description: The rare Democrat in a fabled family of wealthy Republicans, he served 30 years as senator and helped bring health insurance to millions of low-income children.
item.dc:creator: Robert D. McFadden
item.media:credit: Brendan Smialowski for The New York Times
item.media:description: John D. Rockefeller IV on Capitol Hill in 2009. He served five terms as a U.S. senator and two as governor.

item.title: Harriet Hancock, a Force in South Carolina’s Gay Rights Movement, Has Died
item.description: She became an early and leading activist for gay and lesbian rights in a time and place where that was extremely rare. She was 89.
item.dc:creator: Jeré Longman

item.title: Klaus-Michael Kühne Has Died. His Company Played a Dark Role in Nazi Germany.
item.description: As Klaus-Michael Kühne’s business became a global force in container shipping, he resisted demands to document its wartime activities. He was 89.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Kandell
item.media:description: Klaus-Michael Kühne in an undated photo. He was a major philanthropist in culture and education.

item.title: Milton L. Williams Has Died. His Legal Career Touched Major N.Y.C. Events.
item.description: He was executive director of the inquiry into the Attica prison uprising and made a provocative decision in the Central Park jogger case. He died at 93.
item.dc:creator: Sam Roberts
item.media:description: Justice Milton L. Williams was the first Black man appointed as the administrative head of New York City’s vast criminal and civil court system.

item.title: In the Style of P.C. Vey: The Funniest Reader Cartoons We Received
item.description: More than 200 people answered our call for cartoons in the spirit of P.C. Vey. Here are some of the best ones.
item.dc:creator: Amisha Padnani and Michael S. Rosenwald

item.title: Beverly Whipple Has Died. She Introduced the G-Spot to the Mainstream.
item.description: Dr. Whipple studied the female erogenous zone and, with collaborators, wrote a best seller about women’s sexuality. She was 85.
item.dc:creator: Randi Hutter Epstein
item.category: The G Spot and Other Recent Discoveries About Human Sexuality (Book)
item.media:description: Beverly Whipple in 2007. Her book “The G Spot: And Other Recent Discoveries About Human Sexuality,” examined the concept of female sexual pleasure.

item.title: Simon Winchester, Author of ‘The Professor and the Madman,’ Has Died
item.description: He was a geologist who switched careers and became a prolific and adventurous journalist. He died at 82.
item.dc:creator: Alan Cowell
item.category: The Professor and the Madman: A Tale of Murder, Insanity, and the Making of The Oxford English Dictionary (Book)
item.media:description: Simon Winchester spent much of his career reporting for The Guardian.

item.title: John Frieda, Hair-Care Mogul Who Soothed Women’s Curls, Has Died
item.description: He was a celebrity stylist to rock stars and royalty whose blockbuster product, Frizz Ease, changed his fortunes (and women’s hair) forever. He was 75.
item.dc:creator: Penelope Green
item.media:description: John Frieda in 2008. He made his name as a young assistant stylist in Mayfair in the late 1960s and then made a fortune with a blockbuster product called Frizz Ease.

item.title: Senji Kuroi Has Died. He Interpreted ‘the Salaried Soul.’
item.description: In books and essays, he captured the unease beneath Japan’s economic miracle and wrote about everyday people who might never appear in headlines.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Kandell
item.media:credit: The Asahi Shimbun, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Senji Kuroi in 1972. He published dozens of novels, short-story collections and essays, earning major Japanese literary prizes.

item.title: Juan Atkins Has Died. He Helped Invent Techno Music.
item.description: He combined the futurism of Kraftwerk with the funk of George Clinton to arrive at techno, making Detroit a capital of the genre. He was 64.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams
item.media:description: Juan Atkins performing at the Electronic Music Awards in 2017. Rolling Stone wrote that he “invented techno, full stop — he conceived it and named it.”

item.title: Herbert Blomstedt, Low-Key, Long-Performing Maestro, Dies at 99
item.description: He never achieved the celebrity of more glamorous colleagues, but drew acclaim as he remained at the podium until virtually the end of his long life.
item.dc:creator: Vivien Schweitzer
item.media:credit: Richard Termine for The New York Times
item.media:description: Herbert Blomstedt leading the New York Philharmonic in 2012. His reputation only improved as he passed 90, then 95, well after most maestros have retired.
